STANZA I
To God I made my sorrows known
To God I made my sorrows known,
From God I sought relief;
In long complaints before his throne
I pour'd out all my grief.
The psalm it sets
Watts made this hymn from Psalm 142, "in the language of the New Testament": a paraphrase, not a translation. The line that comes closest to it is marked.

1I cry aloud to the LORD; I lift my voice to the LORD for mercy. 2I pour out my complaint before Him; I reveal my trouble to Him. 3Although my spirit grows faint within me, You know my way. Along the path I travel they have hidden a snare for me. 4Look to my right and see; no one attends to me. There is no refuge for me; no one cares for my soul. … 3 more verses PSALM 142 · ITS FIRST VERSES · BEREAN STANDARD BIBLE READ PSALM 142
From my sad prison set me free, Then shall I praise thy Name, And holy men shall join with me Thy kindness to proclaim. STANZA VI
Its place in the book
Watts's psalms run from Psalm 1 to Psalm 150, several settings to many psalms: 367 hymns. This is number 142. Point at a tick to see the hymn; click it to open that hymn.
